# Treemaps {#sec-treemaps} ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="simple"} ## Theme: `theme_j2me()` Graphs in this chapter use `fmggp2::theme_j2me()`, built from a Nokia N73 running a J2ME app: a black phone background, a silver frame, a pale screen panel, Ushahidi red, tan, brown, and black marks, and an Arial Narrow title. ::: :::: {.callout-note collapse="false" icon=false}
::: {.cell layout-align="right"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](treemaps_files/figure-html/full_code_display-1.png){fig-align='right' width=60% height=60%} ::: ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #02577A;"} **Requirements:** ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"} **✅ at least two categorical variables** ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"} **✅ a numeric variable of counts (for each level of the categorical variables)** ::: :::: ## Description Treemaps display proportionally divided rectangular hierarchies for levels of categorical variables. The layout consists of 'squarified' tiles, which display the relative contribution of each categorical value to the overall graph space. We'll build a treemap using the [`treemapify` package.](http://wilkox.org/treemapify/) Also check out the [mosaic plots](mosaic_plots.qmd) chapter. ## Set up ::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"} **PACKAGES:** ::: Install packages. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} # pak::pak("wilkox/treemapify") library(treemapify) library(ggplot2) library(dplyr) # for tibble() and data manipulation library(tidyr) # for expand_grid() ``` ::: ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"} **DATA:** ::: In the early to mid 2000s, most mobile phone games were small J2ME (Java ME) apps that a phone downloaded over the air. Most were bought from the carrier's deck (the games menu on the operator's portal). They held on until the iPhone App Store and Android Market replaced them. We'll simulate one year of downloads for six made up titles in three genres. Each title gets a `yearly_rate` (the downloads we'd expect in a year) and a `deck_share` (the part of those downloads bought through the carrier deck instead of directly from the publisher's site). `tidyr::expand_grid()` creates a row for each title in each `channel`, `lambda` splits the yearly rate between the two channels, and `rpois()` draws the downloads. Setting the seed with `set.seed()` means you'll get the same downloads every time you run the code below. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} set.seed(2003) # same downloads every time the code runs j2me_downloads <- tibble( genre = c("Puzzle", "Puzzle", "Racing", "Racing", # three genres, two games each "Sports", "Sports"), title = c("Block Drop", "Gem Swap", "Street Rally", "Moto Sprint", # six games "Pocket Soccer", "Pro Bowling"), yearly_rate = c(1800, 900, 2400, 700, 1200, 1000), # average downloads per year deck_share = c(0.80, 0.40, 0.35, 0.60, 0.55, 0.50) # share sold through the carrier's menu ) |> tidyr::expand_grid(channel = c("Carrier deck", "Direct")) |> # each game in both channels mutate( lambda = yearly_rate * if_else(channel == "Carrier deck", deck_share, 1 - deck_share), # average downloads in each channel downloads = rpois(n(), lambda = lambda) # download counts around each average ) |> select(genre, title, channel, lambda, downloads) glimpse(j2me_downloads) #> Rows: 12 #> Columns: 5 #> $ genre "Puzzle", "Puzzle", "Puzzle", … #> $ title "Block Drop", "Block Drop", "G… #> $ channel "Carrier deck", "Direct", "Car… #> $ lambda 1440, 360, 360, 540, 840, 1560… #> $ downloads 1493, 346, 387, 539, 849, 1549… ``` ::: ::: ## Distribution A treemap nests counts inside counts: channels inside titles, and titles inside genres. Every tile's area is a share of the total downloads, so the question behind the graph is "how much of the whole does each piece take up?" Below we'll move from the downloads, to a picture, to the formula. ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **COUNT IT:** ::: Start with the rows for Block Drop and Street Rally. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} j2me_downloads |> filter(title %in% c("Block Drop", "Street Rally")) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ::: Each simulated count (`downloads`) lands within a few percent of the rate we gave `rpois()` (`lambda`). Block Drop got most of its downloads through the carrier deck, while Street Rally got most of its downloads directly. Adding up the counts inside each genre gives the genre totals, and dividing by the overall total turns them into the shares the treemap draws. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} j2me_downloads |> group_by(genre) |> summarise(downloads = sum(downloads), expected = sum(lambda)) |> mutate(share = round(downloads / sum(downloads), 3)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **DRAW IT:** ::: A bar model shows the hierarchy one level at a time. Each genre is a bar, each title is a part of its genre's bar, and each part is split by channel. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} ggplot(j2me_downloads, aes(x = downloads, y = title, fill = channel)) + geom_col() + facet_grid(genre ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") + labs(x = "Downloads", y = NULL, fill = "Channel") + theme(legend.position = "bottom") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](treemaps_files/figure-html/draw_bar_model_treemap-1.png){width=100%} ::: ::: ::: A treemap takes the same parts and packs them into one rectangle. Below, the silver borders outline the genres, the black borders outline the titles, and the red and tan fills split each title by channel. The Block Drop tile is about four fifths carrier deck downloads, and the Street Rally tile is mostly direct downloads. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} ggplot(j2me_downloads, aes(area = downloads, fill = channel, subgroup = genre, subgroup2 = title)) + treemapify::geom_treemap() + treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup2_border(color = "#15110E", size = 3) + treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup2_text(color = "#FFFFFF", place = "center", min.size = 0, family = "sans") + treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup_border(color = "#9A9791", size = 6) + labs(fill = "Channel") + theme(legend.position = "bottom") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](treemaps_files/figure-html/draw_treemap-1.png){width=100%} ::: ::: ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **NAME IT:** ::: Each title and channel count comes from a [Poisson distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poisson_distribution): $$ N_{\text{title, channel}} \sim \text{Poisson}(\lambda_{\text{title, channel}}) $$ Poisson counts have a useful property for treemaps: the sum of independent Poisson counts is also Poisson, with a rate equal to the sum of the rates. So each genre total is $\text{Poisson}(\sum \lambda)$: 2,700 for puzzle, 3,100 for racing, and 2,200 for sports. The standard deviation of a Poisson count is $\sqrt{\lambda}$, so its relative wobble is $\sqrt{\lambda} / \lambda = 1 / \sqrt{\lambda}$. For the Block Drop carrier deck tile ($\lambda = 1{,}440$) that's under 3%, which is why the treemap's tiles barely change shape from one simulation to the next. Try dividing every `yearly_rate` by 100 and the small tiles start to jump around. ## Grammar ::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"} **CODE:** ::: - Create labels with `labs()` - Initialize the graph with `ggplot()` and provide `data` - Map the `downloads` to `area`, `channel` to `fill` and `label`, `genre` to `subgroup`, and `title` to `subgroup2` - Add `geom_treemap()` - Add `geom_treemap_text()` - `place`: this controls where the boxes start - `color`: text color - `min.size`: the minimum font size (when re-sizing) - `alpha`: opacity - `fontface`: `italic`/`bold` - `family`: `"sans"`/`"sansserif"`/`"mono"` ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} labs_treemap <- labs( title = "J2ME downloads 2005", caption = "Simulated data", fill = "Channel") ggp2_treemap <- ggplot(j2me_downloads, aes(area = downloads, fill = channel, label = channel, subgroup = genre, subgroup2 = title)) + treemapify::geom_treemap() + treemapify::geom_treemap_text( place = "bottomright", color = "#FFFFFF", min.size = 0, alpha = 0.90, fontface = "italic", family = "sans") ggp2_treemap + labs_treemap ``` ::: ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"} **GRAPH:** ::: ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell layout-nrow="1"} ```{.r .cell-code} labs_treemap <- labs( title = "J2ME downloads 2005", caption = "Simulated data", fill = "Channel") ggp2_treemap <- ggplot(j2me_downloads, aes(area = downloads, fill = channel, label = channel, subgroup = genre, subgroup2 = title)) + treemapify::geom_treemap() + treemapify::geom_treemap_text( place = "bottomright", color = "#FFFFFF", min.size = 0, alpha = 0.90, fontface = "italic", family = "sans") ggp2_treemap + labs_treemap ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](treemaps_files/figure-html/create_graph_treemap-1.png){width=100% height=100%} ::: ::: ::: ## More info `treemapify` has multiple options for building treemaps. We cover a few of these below, but you should check out the [package vignette](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/treemapify/vignettes/introduction-to-treemapify.html). ### Subgroup 2 `ggplot2` builds layers in the order they're written, so it's [advised](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/treemapify/vignettes/introduction-to-treemapify.html) to build the subgroups in order from "*from deepest to shallowest*", with `subgroup2` first (ending on `subgroup`) - Add `geom_treemap_subgroup2_border()` - Set the `size` and `color` - Add `geom_treemap_subgroup2_text()` - `place`: this controls where the boxes start - `color`: text color - `min.size`: the minimum font size (when re-sizing) - `alpha`: opacity - `fontface`: `italic`/`bold` - `family`: `"sans"`/`"sansserif"`/`"mono"` See full list of arguments [here](http://wilkox.org/treemapify/). ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell layout-nrow="1"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggp2_tm_subgroup <- ggp2_treemap + treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup2_border( color = "#15110E", size = 4.0) + treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup2_text( place = "center", alpha = 0.75, color = "#FFFFFF", min.size = 0, family = "sans") ggp2_tm_subgroup + labs_treemap ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](treemaps_files/figure-html/code_graph_treemap_sgb-1.png){width=100% height=100%} ::: ::: ::: ### Subgroup - Add `geom_treemap_subgroup_border()` - Set the `size` and `color` - Add `geom_treemap_subgroup_text()` - `place`: this controls where the boxes start - `color`: text color - `min.size`: the minimum font size (when re-sizing) - `alpha`: opacity - `fontface`: `italic`/`bold` - `family`: `"sans"`/`"sansserif"`/`"mono"` ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell layout-nrow="1"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggp2_tm_subgroup2 <- ggp2_tm_subgroup + treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup_border( color = "#9A9791", size = 4) + treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup_text( place = "topleft", alpha = 0.65, grow = TRUE, color = "#FFFFFF", min.size = 0, family = "mono", fontface = "bold") ggp2_tm_subgroup2 + labs_treemap ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](treemaps_files/figure-html/code_graph_tmap_sgb_2-1.png){width=100% height=100%} ::: ::: :::
